name: Murusapa
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 7 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Capell, A. 1951. Languages of Bogia District, New Guinea. Oceania 22(2): 130-147; sec. 7 'Murusapa', pp. 143-147. doi:10.1002/j.1834-4461.1951.tb00554.x
catalog_locator: pp. 143-144 (the passage begins at the foot of p. 143; the stress sentence is on p. 144), sec. '7. Murusapa'; archive.org microfilm scan of Oceania 22(2), pp. 71-72
catalog_quote: Closed syllables are common and consonant combinations are frequent. Only those with homorganic nasals or stop +w can occur initially or finally, but almost any two consonants can meet within a word. Stress tends to be antepenultimate but is by no means regularly so. Vowel length is noticeable but does not appear to be phonemic.

Surrounding section read (pp. 143-145): p…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Moresada (Murusapa) falls by tendency on the antepenultimate syllable, but the tendency is explicitly said to be irregular ('by no means regularly so'); no conditioning for the exceptions is given. Capell's stress-marked vocabulary (Oceania 22(3): 201-205) shows mostly initial stress on trisyllables ('imbugun, 'takuyom, 'indjayam) alongside penult/final cases (a'nayam, a'sasap, u'gwap). Vowel length non-phonemic; no mention of tone.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the blanket hedge 'by no means regularly so'; no lexical or morphological conditioning stated. Z'graggen 1971: 6-7 independently declined to mark stress in the Madang languages because 'the stress patterning has not been well established yet'.
new_statements.domain_note: Survey-level sketch from brief 1950 fieldwork; statement refers to words as elicited (citation forms in a vocabulary and short sentences); no word-vs-phrase distinction drawn.
new_statements.identity_note: Capell's 'Murusapa' is Moresada (more1258, iso msx): Glottolog lists Murusapa/Murisapa/Murusapa-Sarewa as alternative names, Z'graggen 1971: 57 equates Holtker's 'Murusapa-Sarewa' and Capell's Murusapa with his Moresada (village Moresada), and Daniels 2015: 11 states Capell 'called [Moresada] Murusapa'. Single-village language (c. 160-200 speakers in 1969); no dialect issue.

sources.note: Full grammar of the closest sister language (Ikundun/Anamuxra, 66% lexicostatistical with Moresada per Z'graggen 1971); its stress chapter is the nearest modern comparandum for the Pomoikan family, though it is not Moresada itself (glottocode anam1248/ikun1238).

sources.note: Nothing on Moresada stress; p. 11 states Capell (1951: 143-147) is the only work on Moresada outside Z'graggen's wordlists ('published some grammatical notes and a brief text on Moresada (which he called Murusapa)').
